Devin: Hey team — getting 400s when calling the create-invoice tool. Error: \"tool_args_parse_error: Unexpected token '\\' in JSON at position 0\". Started after we bumped the client lib.
Maya: Can you paste the exact request (curl or SDK snippet)?
Devin: Sure, here's the curl we used:
```\ncurl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{\n    \"model\":\"redwood-chat-1\",\n    \"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"create invoice\"}],\n    \"tool_call\":{\"name\":\"create-invoice\",\"arguments\":\"{'amount': 1000, 'currency':'USD',}\"}\n  }'\n```
Maya: Ah — looks like `arguments` was sent as a string that contains single quotes + a trailing comma. Our tool-args parsing expects strict JSON (double quotes, no trailing commas). If you send `arguments` as a JSON object it should work. Example: `\"arguments\": {\"amount\":1000, \"currency\":\"USD\"}`
Devin: We build the string in Ruby and interpolation produced the single quotes: `invoice_args = "{'amount': #{amt}, 'currency':'USD',}"` — not great hindsight.
Samir: Reproduced locally. Server side log: `JSON.parse` error -> \"Unexpected token ' in JSON at 0\". Request_id=rcw-9f3a. The code path expects either a proper JSON object or a JSON string with double quotes. Trailing comma also blows up many parsers.
Maya: Short-term workarounds: 1) send `arguments` as a native object (preferred), 2) if you must send a string, ensure you generate it with double quotes and no trailing comma (`JSON.generate` in Ruby), 3) as a last resort use a pre-send sanitizer.
Samir: Example fixes for Ruby:
```ruby
# preferred: send a real object
payload[:tool_call] = { name: \"create-invoice\", arguments: { amount: 1000, currency: \"USD\" } }
# or explicitly serialize to strict JSON
payload[:tool_call][:arguments] = JSON.generate({ amount: 1000, currency: \"USD\" })
```
Samir: We considered adding lenient parsing (accept single quotes/strip trailing commas) but that can mask client bugs and create ambiguity/injection risks. Plan: open an internal ENG ticket to prototype a feature-flagged lenient parser in sandbox only, plus docs guidance. I'll file the ticket.
Maya: Filed support ticket SUP-4321, added the Ruby snippet to the reply and recommended switching to JSON.generate. Also asked for confirm when fixed.
Devin: Switched to `JSON.generate` and retested — create-invoice now returns 200 and the invoice id. Thanks! :tada:
support-bot: Ticket SUP-4321 marked awaiting-customer-confirmation.
Maya: Great — closing after one more confirmation. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
